subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a one-click cross-machine browser relay path, wait for a generic browser-backend/plugin API, or formally retire the legacy extension relay use case?
rationale: The regression is source-reproducible, but restoring browser control across extension, gateway, and network boundaries is a product and security decision that automation cannot safely choose by widening a driver enum.

options.title: Design vetted relay/API path
options.body: Keep the issue open and route it through a maintainer-approved browser-backend or extension-bridge design with security review, migration, docs, and proof.

options.title: Wait for generic backend seam
options.body: Track this issue behind the broader browser backend plugin interface and solve the relay use case only after that public contract exists.

options.title: Retire relay use case
options.body: Document that legacy cross-machine extension relay is no longer supported and point managed-hosting users to node host or remote CDP alternatives.

recommendation.title: Design vetted relay/API path
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and route it through a maintainer-approved browser-backend or extension-bridge design with security review, migration, docs, and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: PR 47893 is the strongest merged provenance for the removal and migration behavior at the center of this issue.
